subject: Dedicated capacity prepay — delivery timeline & term options
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@quanticahealth.com>, Tom Hansen <tom.hansen@quanticahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity prepay — proposed delivery timeline & term options

Hi Ellen / Tom,

Thanks again for the detailed walkthrough last week. Per our conversation, attached is a concise term sheet (Quantica_Redwood_TermSheet_v2.pdf) and a draft SOW that lays out delivery windows and an initial ramp proposal for Redwood Dedicated capacity. High level:

- Option A (Annual prepay, 1-year): Upfront payment for 80 GPUs equivalent (A100-80 equivalent); 12% prepay discount; ramp to full throughput in Q3.
- Option B (Multi-year, 2-year): Year1 = 40 GPUs reserved, Year2 = 120 GPUs reserved (phased); 18% blended discount across term; annual invoicing with committed prepay in year 1 and optional true-up at year end.
- Option C (Multi-year, 3-year): More gradual ramp (20 / 60 / 140 GPUs) with 22% blended discount and onboarding credits for dedicated on-prem setup.

Key flexibility items called out in the doc: regional substitution allowance (move reserved capacity between us-west and us-east once per year), limited carry-forward of unused TPM credits within the same contract year, and an overage rate schedule.

We intentionally kept Year1 commitments smaller in the multi-year options to match your anticipated product ramp. I included two ramp schedules in the SOW (linear vs. staged burst model) and flagged where we can insert a 90-day ramp window if you need more time to provision.

Can you review and tell me: 1) which term length you prefer, 2) whether you need a more conservative Year1 minimum, and 3) any procurement/legal must-haves we should fold into the DocuSign. Happy to jump on a quick call next week.

Thanks,

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0128

Attachments:
- Quantica_Redwood_TermSheet_v2.pdf (term sheet, pricing table)
- SOW_Quantica_Dedicated_2026.docx (delivery windows & milestones)
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@quanticahealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Hansen <tom.hansen@quanticahealth.com>, procurement@quanticahealth.com
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity prepay — proposed delivery timeline & term options

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the clear summary and the docs. A few quick questions from our side after an internal review:

1) Year1 sizing: our go-to-market will only need ~25–30 GPUs in the first 6 months. Can we start with a lower Year1 commit (20–40 GPUs) and then have the remainder kick in as a scheduled ramp?
2) Overage / credits: If we underutilize Year1 reserved TPM/GPU, can those credits be applied as one-time credits against Year2 invoice instead of being fully forfeited?
3) Discount: The 22% for the 3-year looks attractive — would you consider an incremental 1–2% improvement if we convert to fully prepaid annual invoices instead of annual invoicing (i.e., full prepay at contract signing)?
4) SLA / credits: our procurement asks for a more explicit monthly latency SLA and financial credits tied to sustained SLA misses.

Also routing a question to procurement: please indicate if you need Redwood to adopt Quantica-specific SOC evidence submission timelines (we occasionally have 10-day windows).

Can you push an updated term sheet that reflects: (a) a lower Year1 commit option, (b) explicit carry-forward mechanics for up to 25% unused Year1 capacity, and (c) an optional fully-prepaid 3-year pricing line? If possible, highlight the legal clauses we should expect to see changed.

Best,
Ellen Park
Head of ML Ops, Quantica Health
ellen.park@quanticahealth.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@quanticahealth.com>, Tom Hansen <tom.hansen@quanticahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2026 10:13:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity prepay — proposed delivery timeline & term options

Ellen — great questions. Quick responses inline, and attached is an amended term sheet that implements the options you asked for. See Quantica_Redwood_TermSheet_v2 (updated table on page 2) and the SOW where I annotated the ramp windows.

1) Year1 sizing: Yes — we can add a Lower Year1 Commit addendum. Concrete proposal: Year1 = 30 GPUs reserved (minimum), with quarterly scheduled increases of +10 GPUs starting in Q3 to hit the Year2 target. If you need a 90-day ramp (no penalties), we can bake that into the SOW.

2) Overage / credits: We will allow carry-forward of up to 25% of unused Year1 committed TPM/GPU as a one-time credit applied to Year2 invoice. Amounts beyond that will follow our overage pricing. This is reflected under Section 4.3 of the term sheet.

3) Discount / prepay mechanics: Fully-prepaid 3-year option (paid at sign) would qualify for an extra 2% discount on top of the 22% (i.e., 24% effective). Alternatively, annual prepay for each year gets +1% per year. Both options are in the updated pricing table.

4) SLA / credits: We can include monthly latency SLOs with tiered financial credits tied to sustained misses. I flagged the specific SLA language for your legal team to review.

Regional substitution: we can permit one region swap per year as long as the SKU parity is maintained (A100-equivalent to A100-equivalent). We'll add a clause to the SOW to make this explicit.

Next steps I propose: 1) you confirm which payment cadence (fully prepaid 3-year vs annual prepay), 2) we finalize SOW ramp dates, 3) we send for procurement/legal review and DocuSign. I added DocuSign & HubSpot links in the footer so procurement can see the draft.

Marissa
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachments: Updated Quantica_Redwood_TermSheet_v2.pdf (pricing table updated), SOW_Quantica_Dedicated_2026.docx (annotated ramp windows)
From: Tom Hansen <tom.hansen@quanticahealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ellen Park <ellen.park@quanticahealth.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity prepay — delivery timeline & term options

Marissa / Ellen,

Thanks — a few procurement/legal clarifications from our finance side:

- Payment schedule: if we do the fully-prepaid 3-year option, we need an escrowed schedule or proof-of-service milestones tied to partial releases. Can Redwood accept a milestone-based release of the prepaid funds (e.g., 30% on sign, 40% at first fully provisioned cluster, 30% after final acceptance)?
- Capacity substitution: we appreciate the one region swap clause. Can you confirm whether we can split our reserved capacity across regions at contract signing (e.g., 60% us-west, 40% us-east) and then re-balance once per year?
- SLA credits: acceptable if there is a clear cap on credits (no more than 25% of monthly invoice) and an escalation path.

If you can incorporate those points into the SOW and term sheet, we can run it through legal next week. Also loop in your enablement team for an onboarding checklist — we'll need an inventory of integration points (network, KMS, audit logs).

Tom Hansen
CFO, Quantica Health
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2026 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: proposed concessions for Quantica deal

Marissa / Vivek — quick internal note before we send the next revision to Quantica:

I recommend we concede the following to close the deal while protecting economics:

- Accept Year1 = 30 GPUs minimum with quarterly scheduled increases (as Marissa proposed).
- Carry-forward cap at 25% of Year1 unused capacity into Year2 as one-time credit.
- For fully-prepaid 3-year: additional 2% discount, but require milestone-based escrow release (30/40/30) as Tom requested.
- Offer a one-time onboarding credit of $25k (applied against Year1 invoice) to cover integration effort.

Proposed legal language bullets to hand to counsel:
- "Milestone release schedule for prepaid amounts: defined in SOW Exhibit B; release contingent on provisioning and acceptance criteria."
- "Capacity substitution: one annual region rebalancing allowed, provided aggregate reserved capacity remains unchanged."

If Vivek signs off, I'll include this exact language in the next term-sheet pass and trigger a DocuSign envelope with those exhibits attached.

Karthik
Director, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@quanticahealth.com>, Tom Hansen <tom.hansen@quanticahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2026 15:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity prepay — delivery timeline & term options

Ellen / Tom — thank you. Following internal alignment with Karthik and Vivek, attached is the updated term sheet and SOW that incorporate the concessions we discussed. Summary of agreed points:

- Agreed payment options: fully-prepaid 3-year at 24% effective discount (2% extra for full-prepay) with milestone-based release (30% sign, 40% provisioning, 30% final acceptance) OR annual prepay with +1% per-year incentive.
- Ramp: Year1 = 30 GPUs minimum, quarterly scheduled increases of +10 GPUs starting Q3 to reach Year2 target. Option for 90-day no-penalty ramp window included.
- Carry-forward: up to 25% of Year1 unused capacity may be credited toward Year2 as a one-time credit.
- Regional substitution: split at signing allowed (e.g., 60/40), with one annual region rebalancing allowed thereafter.
- SLA credits: monthly SLOs with a max credit cap of 25% of monthly invoice; escalation path included in Annex A.
- Commercial concession: one-time onboarding credit of $25,000 applied to Year1 invoice.

Next steps: I will upload the final documents to DocuSign (link below) and create the HubSpot deal update. Please confirm which payment cadence you want (fully-prepaid 3-year vs annual prepay) so we can populate the invoice terms and prepare counsel's exhibits. If agreed, we aim to have executed contract by 2026-04-16 to meet your Q2 provisioning window.

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/envelope/ABCDEF123456
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/67890

Thanks — looking forward to getting you onboarded.

—
Marissa Cole
